strategies.name: vwap_mean_reversion_session_extremes
strategies.entry_summary: During a session, look for price to be extended away from the session VWAP into the first, second, or third standard deviation bands, then enter in the direction of reversion back toward VWAP when those outer bands are reached or after a break/retest of the VWAP or bands confirms the move. variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to get to at least the first or second standard deviation, then break and retest VWAP or the band before

variants.target_note: target the central VWAP for price rebalancing

strategies.name: vwap_support_resistance_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: Trade in the direction of the prevailing session move when price breaks and holds above or below the VWAP or its bands, treating the VWAP and standard deviation lines as dynamic support or resistance for continuation entries. The speaker describes buying after price bounces off VWAP or pulling back
strategies.exit_summary: Exit into the next VWAP band, back at VWAP, or at the next reaction level created by the standard deviation bands; the line can also be used as a target when price rebalances after extension.

variants.variant_label: Long continuation off VWAP or lower bands
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to break VWAP, retest it, and then resume higher; or buy when price bounces from VWAP as support
variants.target_note: use the second or third standard deviation as target, or VWAP if entering from an extension

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to test VWAP or upper bands as resistance and then continue lower
variants.target_note: target the lower deviations / VWAP as the rebalancing point

enumeration_note: The transcript teaches two distinct VWAP-based skeletons: mean-reversion off premium/discount extremes and continuation using VWAP/bands as dynamic support-resistance. Within each, the exact deviation band and session example vary as compatible configuration.
